turns.text: A hum arrives low in the teeth before it arrives anywhere else, riding up through catwalk grating into all four paws at once — not one hum but three, stacked slightly wrong against each other, and the wrongness between them has a taste, faint ozone-sour, the way a held battery tastes if a tongue is foolish enough to check. Ears haven't decided which way to point yet. Nothing has moved. Everything is already listening.

the maintenance catwalk runs the spine of the monorail line, bolted iron slats slick with a night's worth of drizzle, cable trunking humming its three overlapping tones dead level with your chest. below, the rails themselves sit dark and waiting, twin lines of brushed steel catching what little glow spills sideways off a arcology facade three blocks off. wind funnels down the track corridor in slow pulses, carrying diesel, ionized rain, and — thinner, underneath — the particular burnt-plastic smell of a relay box that's run hot too many nights running.

That burnt-plastic thread pulls harder than the hum does. Paws find the rail of the catwalk and follow it, low, weight rolling heel to toe out of old habit rather than present danger. The three tones don't resolve into one as the relay box comes into view — if anything they split further, a fourth thread joining from somewhere overhead, sharp and yellow-tasting where the others ran blue.

the relay box sits bolted to a support strut, casing warped slightly outward from internal heat, a single status light stuttering between green and a green that's almost not green at all. overhead, the fourth thread traces back to a transit speaker, dead to human ears but still broadcasting on a band nothing down here should be able to catch — and yet the whiskers catch it anyway, a jingle stub looping too fast to be words: buy buy buy buy, chewed down to pure rhythm.

None of this sorts into names, only into flavors and weights, the way it always fails to sort no matter how many nights get spent chasing it. A kittenhood surfaces uninvited — sun on a different fur, a different set of paws, gone before it can be questioned, same as always. Nose presses to the relay casing anyway. Whatever's wrong in there is worth knowing regardless of whose memory just walked through.

the casing gives off heat in slow waves, and behind it, half-visible through a warped seam, a spider's-web of hair-thin filament wiring pulses in time with the stuttering light — not damage, exactly, more like something's been living in there, threading its own circuit through the district's circuit, patient and small and uninterested in being found.

.-=====-.
     ( [0]  .. )
      '-==Y==-'
       |  |  |
   ...picking through the neon rain...

A claw finds the warped seam's edge, testing rather than committing. Somewhere down the track a rail sings — not the hum from before, something new, metal remembering a weight that hasn't arrived yet. Ears swivel off the relay box entirely, toward the singing rail, toward the only thing on this whole catwalk that means move now instead of look closer.

the rail's singing climbs fast, resolving into a headlight two curves down the line, silent, magnetic, closing distance with none of the noise a wheeled thing would make. the catwalk's safety rail sits a clean jump above the track bed — plenty of clearance, plenty of time, the kind of danger that's only danger to something that hesitates.

No hesitation in the legs, whatever's happening in the head. Up onto the rail in one motion, balance found and kept as the monorail car finally makes sound — not a roar, a pressure, air shoved ahead of it in a wall that flattens ears and fur both. It passes a body-length below, close enough that its window-light strobes the whole catwalk white-yellow-white.

the strobing window-light carries faces inside it, blurred to nothing at this speed, and for the half-second it takes to pass, every one of those windows tastes like something distinct and separate — cold coffee, wet wool, a stranger's tired perfume — gone as fast as it arrived, the car already shrinking toward the next curve, its wake rocking the catwalk on its bolts.

,--.
       ( o.o)__
        '--'   \___
                 \  \__/\_/\
                  \_(  o.o  )
                     > ^ < (watching the towers blink)

Down off the rail once the wake settles, legs slower to agree than they were going up. Every one of those borrowed tastes sits stacked now behind the tongue, cold coffee and wet wool and someone's perfume all still there, refusing to file themselves anywhere useful. Half of what this body carries around was never its own to begin with. Keep moving anyway. That's the only trick that's ever worked.

the catwalk ladders down at its far end into an equipment platform stacked with spare rail, and past the platform's edge the district opens into rooftops running downhill toward the market strip. two roofs over, a shape crosses fast and low along a gutter line, fur singed pale in one long stripe down its flank, gone into a stairwell gap before it's worth calling more than a shape at all — whatever business it has with that scorched fur, it isn't slowing down to share it.

Ears track the scorched-fur shape half a beat, filing it under not mine to chase, and let the equipment platform's ladder take the weight instead. Rung by rung, the burnt-plastic smell from the relay box fades out behind, replaced by something warmer, oil and standing water, the ordinary smell of ground getting closer.

the platform lets out onto a loading yard stacked three crates high, a drone-broadcast crackling thin off a pole speaker, half swallowed by static — some looping bounty figure nobody's collected, a name that means nothing to anyone not already hunting it, the numbers ticking up out of habit more than threat. rain has thinned to almost nothing, more mist now than fall, beading along crate edges without ever quite dripping.

The bounty-static passes through the same as the drone earlier did, noted and discounted, nothing in it worth the attention it's asking for. What matters is the crate stack's shadow, deep enough to sit in, and a food-smell thin but real drifting off it — someone's dropped ration, cooling, unclaimed.

the ration sits half-unwrapped on a pallet corner, foil peeled back by something with less patience than teeth require, and underneath the food-smell runs a second thread, faint, animal, recent — not threat, not challenge, just another set of paws that stopped here first and moved on without finishing the job.

Finish it, then. Teeth close around what's left, foil crinkling, the yard's mist settling cold and fine over fur already damp from the catwalk. The stacked tastes from the monorail's windows are fading now under this one plain, real flavor — the first thing all night that belongs entirely to this mouth and no other.

the yard holds still around the eating, crate-shadow deep enough to swallow most of the mist-light, the pole speaker's bounty loop finally cutting to dead static and staying there. far off, the monorail sings through another curve, distant now, its three overlapping engine-tones thinning into just one more sound among all the rest the district makes at this hour — unhurried, indifferent, already forgetting the weight it carried past a few minutes ago.
